passages.original: Quam flebiles voces exprimit in quadam ad Atticum epistula iam victo patre Pompeio, adhuc filio in Hispania fracta arma refovente ! " Quid agam," inquit, " hic, quaeris? Moror in Tusculano meo semiliber." Alia deinceps adicit, quibus et priorem aetatem complorat et de praesenti queritur et de futura desperat. Semiliberum se dixit Cicero.
passages.english: What tearful words he utters in a certain letter to Atticus, when Pompey the father had already been defeated and the son was still reviving his broken arms in Spain! "You ask," he says, "what I am doing here? I am lingering in my Tusculan villa, half-free." He then adds other things, in which he both laments his earlier life and complains about the present and despairs of the future. Cicero called himself half-free.
passages.notes: The passage concerns Cicero, who is named only at the end; the preceding text presumably introduced him. 'Fracta arma refovente': the son (Gnaeus Pompeius the younger) was renewing the broken forces of the Pompeian side in Spain.
